_status: The learner guide's eight Try it 2.3 messages (Module 2 learner guide, pages 12, 13 and 19), drawn as fictional samples. Verdicts and warning signs follow the guide's model answers. Every name, address and domain is invented: .example domains can never be real.

messages.subject: DICT Advisory: verify your government mailbox [[c2|within 24 hours]]
messages.body:
Dear mailbox user,

Under a new security advisory, every government mailbox must be verified. Mailboxes that are not verified will be closed.

Verify my mailbox

cues.text: A look-alike address: **dict-gov-ph.verify-portal.example** is not a .gov.ph domain.
A 24-hour deadline, written to rush you.
A login link. Never sign in from a link in a message.

messages.why: Close it and report it to your IT unit. If you are unsure, call IT on the number you already have.

messages.subject: Invoice 4471
messages.body:
Good afternoon, Dan,

[[c1|We have changed banks.]] Please pay invoice 4471 to our new account [[c2|today]].

Thank you,
Accounts, Northgate Office Supplies

cues.text: A change of bank details: the classic sign of business email compromise.
Urgency: pay today.

messages.why: The address may look right: the supplier's own account may be hijacked. Call the supplier on the number in your files and get a second approval before any bank-detail change.

messages.body: RSSO: your assistance payout [[c2|is on hold]]. [[c3|Update your details]] at [[c1|s.example/rq7Kp]]

cues.text: A short link hides where it really goes.
Pressure about a payout.
A request to update your details by text.

messages.why: Check payout news only through the office's official channels. Report scam texts to 1326.

messages.body: Good morning. [[c1|This is Officer Santos of the cybercrime police.]] Your SIM is linked to a fraud complaint. [[c2|To confirm SIM ownership, call us back and read out the one-time code we just sent to your phone.]] [[c3|If we do not hear from you today, your number will be blocked.]]

cues.text: Authority: anyone can say they are from law enforcement.
A request for a one-time code. Never share a one-time code with anyone.
A threat and a deadline, so you act before you check.

messages.why: Do not call back. Report it to 1326. If you are worried, call the agency on a number you look up yourself.

poster.title: [[c1|Scan to claim your cash aid today.]]
poster.body: Cash aid for residents · scan with your phone
poster.place: [[c2|Taped outside the office: no seal, not on the official notice board]]

messages.body: [[c3|No web address printed under the code]]

cues.text: A reward with a deadline: cash aid today.
An unofficial poster. Who put it up?
The QR code hides where it goes: a claim page that asks for your details.

messages.why: Do not scan it. Check the office's official channels, and tell the staff so they can take it down.

messages.subject: (no subject)
messages.body:
[[c1|Pls review this file urgently]]

Open file

cues.text: Urgency and an unusual tone: no greeting, no context, not how Sol writes.
The link opens a page that asks for your email password. A shared file never needs it.

messages.why: Sol's account may be hijacked. Call Sol on a number you already know before opening anything, and tell your IT unit.

messages.subject: Reminder: privacy training tomorrow, 9:00 AM
messages.body:
Good afternoon, everyone.

A reminder that the privacy training is tomorrow at 9:00 AM in the conference room, [[c3|as announced in the memo on the bulletin board]]. [[c2|No sign-up or reply needed.]]

HR Unit

cues.text: HR's usual address.
No link, no attachment, nothing asked of you.
It matches the memo on the bulletin board: you can check it yourself.

messages.why: A known sender, nothing to click, and every detail can be checked in the office.

messages.body: Q Savings: a purchase of P2,450.00 was made with your debit card on 20 Oct at 2:14 PM. [[c2|If this was not you, call the number on the back of your card.]]

cues.text: Your bank's registered sender name.
No link. It sends you to a number you already have: the one on your card.

messages.why: It asks for nothing and points you to a channel you control: the number on your card, never one in a message.
